requirements:
R1. Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with rustc --edition 2024, std only. All API items below must be pub. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences.

R2. Expose exactly the following callable API (derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq are required on every public API struct and enum):
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WrapError {
    WidthZero,
    WidthTooLarge { width: usize },
    InvalidByte { index: usize, byte: u8 },
}
pub fn wrap(input: &str, width: usize) -> Result<Vec<String>, WrapError>;

R3. Validate configuration before examining input: width == 0 yields WidthZero; otherwise width > 256 yields WidthTooLarge { width }. Width counts output columns including indentation and visible hyphens.

R4. After width validation, scan original input bytes left to right. Only ASCII printable bytes 32..=126, tab (9), LF (10), and CR (13) are allowed. The first other byte yields InvalidByte { index, byte }, with a zero-based byte index; do not partially return output.

R5. Space, tab, LF, and CR are interchangeable separators. Collapse every nonempty run to one word boundary. Leading/trailing separators produce no empty words or lines. Empty or all-separator input returns Ok(vec![]).

R6. A word is a maximal run of nonseparator bytes. Preserve all its printable characters literally, including punctuation, backslash and hyphen; there is no escape syntax.

R7. Maintain a current line initially empty and process words in input order; emitted lines are never revisited. There is no indentation.

R8. At each step consider the unconsumed suffix of the current word. If its length is at most width, append it whole if it fits, using exactly one separating space when the line is nonempty.

R9. If that suffix is at most width but does not fit, emit the current line, then retry the same suffix on an empty line. Never split such a suffix just to fill a partially occupied line.

R10. If the suffix is longer than width and the current line is empty, take its first width bytes as a line and emit it, then retry the remaining suffix.

R11. If the suffix is longer than width and the line is nonempty, compute available = width - current_length - 1 (the 1 reserves a separator).

R12. When available >= 2, append one space and exactly available bytes from the suffix, emit this full line, then retry the remainder. This rule applies only to a suffix longer than width.

R13. When available < 2, emit the current line without consuming any of the suffix and retry it on an empty line. In particular a single available column must be left unused.

R14. A line already containing width bytes is emitted before processing another word. At end of input emit the current line only if nonempty. An exactly divisible long word never creates an extra empty line.

R15. A short tail of a split word remains on the current line and may share it with the next word, subject to the same rules.

R16. Returned strings have no leading or trailing spaces, no newlines, and length at most width. Concatenating their nonspace bytes recovers exactly the input nonseparator bytes in order.
